text: Track 6.1 Hey, Carl! Professor Garcia says another group has chosen our topic for their project. We have to find a different one. Oh no! That was a great topic and we had good ideas about it. What can we look at instead? Well, how about the advantages and disadvantages for businesses of letting their employees work from home? Great idea! Have you got any information about it? Yes, I do. The numbers are really interesting. More people are working from home than before. A recent survey showed that 63% of people work from home at least part of the time. Working from home increased from 20% in 2020 to 28% in 2023. And the technology industry had the most employees working from home – 67%. All this can help businesses save up to 40% on office space costs. Wow! That is amazing! But I don't think I would want to work at home all the time. I like having people to talk to. But how do companies know that their employees are not taking long breaks and wasting time during the day instead of working? Well, they can ask employees to write down the hours they work. Or they can focus on whether the employee is reaching their business goals. In another survey, 48.3% of businesses said that they were in favor of home working because it increased productivity. Really? That surprises me. Well, think about it. The employer sets the goals for what they want the employees to achieve. But the employees can choose how they spend their time during the day. Homeworkers don't waste time traveling. I read that home workers in the U.S. save an average of 55 minutes every day because they don't have to travel to work. So they have more time to exercise more, eat more healthily, and organize their day. One study said that if workers can work from home, they are up to 20% happier. Wow! That's a lot! Great research, Suzy! But I'd also like to find out how much your personality helps you to be successful at home working. For example, you need good skills in how to manage your time. If your home is also where you work, your job could take over your whole life. Yes, you're right. We need to do some research on that.

segments.text: Track 6.1
Hey, Carl!
Professor Garcia says another group has chosen our topic for their project.
We have to find a different one.
Oh no! That was a great topic and we had good ideas about it.
What can we look at instead?
Well, how about the advantages and disadvantages for businesses of letting their employees work from home?
Great idea! Have you got any information about it?
Yes, I do. The numbers are really interesting.
More people are working from home than before.
A recent survey showed that 63% of people work from home at least part of the time.
Working from home increased from 20% in 2020 to 28% in 2023.
And the technology industry had the most employees working from home – 67%.
All this can help businesses save up to 40% on office space costs.
Wow! That is amazing! But I don't think I would want to work at home all the time.
I like having people to talk to.
But how do companies know that their employees are not taking long breaks and wasting time during the day instead of working?
Well, they can ask employees to write down the hours they work.
Or they can focus on whether the employee is reaching their business goals.
In another survey, 48.3% of businesses said that they were in favor of home working because it increased productivity.
Really? That surprises me.
Well, think about it.
The employer sets the goals for what they want the employees to achieve.
But the employees can choose how they spend their time during the day.
Homeworkers don't waste time traveling.
I read that home workers in the U.S. save an average of 55 minutes every day because they don't have to travel to work.
So they have more time to exercise more, eat more healthily, and organize their day.
One study said that if workers can work from home, they are up to 20% happier.
Wow! That's a lot! Great research, Suzy!
But I'd also like to find out how much your personality helps you to be successful at home working.
For example, you need good skills in how to manage your time.
If your home is also where you work, your job could take over your whole life.
Yes, you're right. We need to do some research on that.
